input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: Direction is favourable on the Vendor side: Array has no termination-for-convenience right at all (Sections 13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy and 8.2 exclusivity breach are its only routes), which meets the preferred position. The failure is on our side. The term under Section 13.1 runs product-by-product until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, i.e. many years, yet our at-will exit under 13.2 does not become available until the later of two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products. Through the whole development and pre-launch phase — where our spend and risk are greatest — we have no convenience right (only 13.5 Safety/Efficacy and 13.3 breach), which is the walk-away case of "no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term". The notice period is also redacted, so the fallback 60–90 day band cannot be verified. Redline removes the First Commercial Sale gate and fixes notice at ninety (90) days, which is longer than our preferred thirty (30) days but proportionate given the extensive Article 14 wind-down obligations. Noted but not separately flagged: on a 13.2 exit we bear the transition and ongoing Clinical Study costs (p0647, p0656) and are subject to a post-termination Competing Product restriction (p0492) — these are the real price of convenience and belong to the exclusivity/exit-cost rules rather than a second redline here.

proposal.summary: Remove the First Commercial Sale time-gate on Ono's Section 13.2 at-will termination right and fix the notice period at 90 days
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13.2 only lets us exit at will after First Commercial Sale of both Products, so we are locked into a multi-year term through the entire development phase; our playbook requires a customer convenience right exercisable throughout the term. We have made the right available at any time on ninety (90) days' notice (longer than our usual thirty (30) days) to accommodate the Article 14 wind-down machinery.
